key_insight: Medical LLMs can lose correct answers when misleading context is added, revealing weak epistemic resilience despite strong exam performance.
clinical_relevance: In patient-facing settings, this means high benchmark scores may overstate how safely an LLM will handle deceptive or biased medical information.
method: Built MedMisBench with 10,932 medical questions and 48,889 misleading context-option pairs.
Tested 11 model configurations across medical reasoning, agentic capability, and patient-journey evaluation.
Measured whether models kept original correct answers under injected false context versus baseline questions.
evidence_signal: Across 11 model configurations, accuracy fell from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% with focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked prompts and should not be treated as direct evidence of real-world clinical performance without further external validation.
paper_title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
